cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel the prophet again, and this time it's aimed at one man: Gog of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. God tells Ezekiel to set his face against Gog and prophesy against him. And the message opens with God saying, Behold, I am against you, O Gog.
God says He will turn Gog around, put hooks in his jaws, and bring him out. Friend, that's not a road trip. That's getting TOWED.

cards.question: God says He'll bring Gog out with all his ___.

cards.text: Horses, horsemen in full armor, shields and swords, plus Persia, Cush, Put, Gomer and Beth-togarmah from the far north. The biggest crowd I ever saw in my junk drawer was a pile of rubber bands, and this guy shows up with NATIONS.

cards.question: God tells Gog to get ready and prepare himself and all the company gathered around him.

cards.text: But this won't happen soon. God says after a long time Gog will be summoned, and in the latter years he'll enter a land on the mountains of Israel that had long been desolate.

cards.question: In the latter years, the land Gog enters is one that has recovered from ___.
When Gog enters the land in the latter years, its people are still living as captives in other nations.

cards.text: By then the people are home, and all of them dwell securely. Then Gog and all his troops will go up, advancing like a thunderstorm, like a cloud covering the land.

cards.question: On that day, God says thoughts will arise in Gog's mind and he will devise an evil plan.

cards.text: Gog says he'll come against a quiet people who dwell securely. Friend, when your big master plan is "find the folks minding their own business," that's not a plan.

cards.question: What does Gog say about the land of these quiet people?

answers.text: They live without walls or gates
Their land still lies in ruins

cards.question: What is Gog after when he goes up against this quiet land?

cards.text: Gog isn't the only one watching. Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish see the whole thing, and they have questions.

cards.question: Sheba, Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish ask Gog if he has come to make off with silver and gold.

cards.text: Then God has Ezekiel speak to Gog again: "On that day when My people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not take notice of this?" Oh, Gog is going to notice, friend.

cards.question: Gog comes against Israel out of the far south.

cards.text: A mighty horde, all riding horses, advancing like a cloud covering the land. Then God says the quiet part out loud: in the latter days, He is the One bringing Gog against His land.

cards.question: Why does God say He will bring Gog against His land?

answers.text: So the nations may know Him
So Gog's own people are punished
So Israel's army can be tested

cards.text: Then God asks Gog a question: is he the one God has spoken of in former days?

cards.question: God says He spoke of Gog in former days through His servants, the ___ of Israel.

cards.text: Gog thinks this whole thing was his idea. Nope, those prophets talked about it for YEARS, and now God speaks of the day Gog comes against the land of Israel.

cards.question: When Gog comes against the land of Israel, God says His wrath will flare up.

cards.text: In His zeal and fiery rage, God proclaims what will happen in the land of Israel on that day.

cards.question: God says on that day there will be a great ___ in the land of Israel.
On that day, who does God say will tremble at His presence?

cards.text: God says the mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground. Gog went looking for a land with no walls, and well, friend, now NOBODY has walls.

cards.question: God summons a sword against Gog on all His mountains. What does God say every man's sword will be against?

cards.text: God says He'll judge Gog with plague and bloodshed, and pour out torrents of rain, hailstones, fire and sulfur on him, his troops and the many nations with him. Gog came in like a thunderstorm, and he just ran into a REAL one.

cards.question: When it's all over, God says many nations will know that He is the LORD.

cards.text: God says He will magnify and sanctify Himself and reveal Himself in the sight of many nations. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, but God's word about Gog isn't done yet.

findings.problem: True or false takes 4 of the 8 choice cards in stop 1 (cards 5, 8, 10 and 15). Multiple choice and fill in the blank have 2 each, so true or false dominates the stop by a wide margin. Three of those cards (5, 10, 15) also just restate a verse with True as the answer.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "Then God says the quiet part out loud" is an idiom for someone letting slip a motive they meant to hide. It makes God the target of the joke.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: "Gog thinks this whole thing was his idea" states Gog's thoughts as fact. The text never says what Gog thinks about whose idea it was. It isn't marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: Ezekiel 38:17 is a question: "Are you the one of whom I have spoken in former days...?" The card turns it into a flat statement that the prophets talked about Gog for years ("Nope, those prophets talked about it for YEARS"). That closes what the text leaves as a question.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "flood" is arguably true in the passage. Ezekiel 38:22 says God will "pour out torrents of rain" on Gog and his troops, and a baker could argue that torrents of rain are a flood.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with "Only" ("Only Gog and his troops" and "Only the people of Israel"). The broad answer "Every creature and all mankind" is the odd one out, which gives it away by its wording.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
